output.name: Nethe — the Shag with Wings Out (The Windward Reach)
output.myth: Nethe was a shag who sat on the rock below the cliffs and would not go in when the rain came. She held her wings out to dry, and they were never dry, and she said so, and the other birds laughed at her. Tavo the Gale heard the laughing and came down to see. He blew on her wings until they were nearly dry, then sent a squall to wet them again, because that is his way. Ennu the Kite-Wright was mending a sail on the shingle with a bone awl she was proud of, and she said nothing. She handed Nethe a corner of cloth and showed her how to hold it against the wind so the wet would run off. Hevalu, the Gull Let Go, watched from the north. Mother Hesk marked Nethe down among those who wait. Now when your coat is heavy and your hands are cold, look up. Nethe is there with her wings out, with Ennu's awl shining to the north-east. Wait a little. The rock will be dry in the morning.
output.finding: Find Hevalu, the Gull Let Go, in the northern sky, then look a little over one hand-span (about 22°) straight south of her to see Nethe with her wings out.
